_description:
# Other agents: which tool

- A helper you can talk to, change and remove later: `subagent` (see `aos/agents.json#/subagent`).
- Start, stop or list any agent on the daemon, without making it yours: `agents_ctl` (see `aos/agents.json#/agents_ctl`).
- A new kind of agent: copy a template with `agent_def`, edit the copy with your file tools, then start it with `subagent` (see `aos/agents.json#/agent_def`).
- One task, only the conclusion back: `thought` (see `aos/agents.json#/thought`).

A child runs on the same daemon as you. It does not inherit your brain or your tools: they come from its own definition.

subagent._description: Tool `subagent`: start your own child agents, talk to them, change their tools or brain, stop and remove them; counted against your quota.

agents_ctl._description: Tool `agents_ctl`: aos-agent ctl for any agent on your daemon table (add, rm, ls, state, stop, start ...); no record, no quota.

agent_def._description: Tool `agent_def`: copy a template folder into a new agent definition, or check a definition.

thought._description: The `thought` tool starts a disposable child agent, gives it one task and returns only a short conclusion; the child's tool exchanges do not enter your history. The child definition comes from the call parameter `from`; only when omitted does it use the default in the tool registration's `env.AOS_THOUGHT_FROM`.

subagent._description:
# Your own children: subagent

Tool `subagent` starts agents that are yours. Only agents you started with it are yours: you can talk to them, change their tools, brain, history, hooks and system text, stop and remove them. They count against your quota.

One op per call:

- start: `{"op": "add", "def": "defs/helper", "name": "kid", "ws": "kid"}` (`def` = a definition folder; no definition yet? first `agent_def` `{"op": "new", "template": "agent-fsm", "path": "defs/helper"}`; `ws` = its workspace, relative to yours, created if missing; default = your own)
- list yours: `{"op": "ls"}` (one line per child: NAME STATE WORKSPACE QUEUED REASON, then `children N/MAX`; `"long": true` adds health columns QUEUE RESTARTS COOLDOWN LAST ERROR; `"json": true` = every field as JSON)
- ask and wait: `{"op": "ask", "name": "kid", "text": "what time is it?"}` (waits up to 600 s; `timeout_s` changes it)
- say now, read later: `{"op": "say", "name": "kid", "text": "hello"}`, then `{"op": "listen", "name": "kid"}` (`"last": 3` shows the last 3 without waiting)
- its tools: `{"op": "tools", "name": "kid", "args": {"op": "add", "path": "tools/math"}}`
- its brain: `{"op": "llm", "name": "kid", "args": {"op": "set", "settings": {"model": "fake"}}}`
- its history, its hooks, its system text: `"op": "history"`, `"op": "hook"`, `"op": "system"`
- `{"op": "state", "name": "kid"}`; `stop`/`start`, `sleep`/`wake`, `pause`/`resume` the same way
- remove: `{"op": "rm", "name": "kid"}` (keeps its stack; `"purge": true` deletes it)

`args` is exactly what `self_tools`, `self_llm`, `self_history`, `self_hook` or `self_system` takes (see `aos/me.json`); the change lands on the child, not on you.

Quota and errors: `aos/agents.json#/subagent/errors`.

errors._description: subagent: the quota (max_children in children.json) and what each error means.

subagent.errors:
# subagent: quota and errors

Quota: at most `max_children` children at once (default 4). It is set in `children.json` of your definition; a `children.json` in your own stack overrides it with only the keys you change, like `{"max_children": 2}`. The tool itself records who is yours (in your stack under `tools/subagent/`); do not edit that record.

- `ChildSlotMissing`: your quota is full; nothing was started. `rm` a child you no longer need, or say the limit is reached. Do not retry in a loop.
- `AddRejected ... SlotMissing`: the daemon is full (its judge counts every agent), not your quota. Same: remove one or report.
- `ChildUnknown`: you did not start that agent with this tool. For other agents use `agents_ctl` (you cannot talk to them).
- `ChildMissing`: someone else removed it; it is forgotten now and its slot is free.
- `ChildQueued`: it still waits for a slot and has no stack yet; try again when `ls` shows it.
- `AnswerMissing`: no answer in time. Run `state`: `stopped` with a reason means it crashed (see `aos/status.json`); `running` means it is slow: `listen` later, or with a longer `timeout_s`.
- `ToolMissing`: the `self_*` tool for that op is not installed next to this one.
- `ArgumentsBad`: that op does not take a key you gave, or a value has the wrong type; the message lists what it takes.

Remove children when you are done with them. Nobody removes them for you.

agents_ctl:
# Any agent on the table: agents_ctl

Tool `agents_ctl` is `aos-agent ctl` for any agent on your daemon table, not only yours. It keeps no record and has no quota; whether a call works is up to your permissions and the daemon. It cannot talk to an agent or change its tools or brain: for that, start the agent with `subagent`.

One op per call (the keys are the ctl flags):

- `{"op": "ls"}` (one line per agent: NAME STATE WORKSPACE QUEUED REASON; `"long": true` adds health columns; `"json": true` = every field as JSON)
- `{"op": "state", "name": "worker"}`
- `{"op": "add", "def": "defs/helper", "name": "worker", "ws": "work"}` (same keys as `subagent` add; the agent is not yours afterwards)
- `{"op": "stop", "name": "worker"}` (after this round; `start` = run again)
- `{"op": "sleep", "name": "worker"}` (now; `wake` = back); `pause` / `resume` = hold / go on
- `{"op": "rm", "name": "worker"}` (keeps its stack; `"purge": true` deletes it)
- `{"op": "where", "name": "worker", "what": "ws"}` (its workspace; default: its stack)
- `{"op": "who"}` (which agent you are)

Rules:

- Relative paths start at your workspace.
- It works on agents that are not yours too, `rm` included, as far as your permissions go. If you remove one of your own `subagent` children here, `subagent` forgets it on its next call and the slot frees.
- `InstanceMissing`: no such name on the table; `ls` first. `InstanceExists`: the name is taken; pick another. `AddRejected`: the daemon refused, often because it is full. `PhaseBad`: wrong phase for that op (for example `start` on a sleeping agent: use `wake`); run `state` first. `DaemonMissing`: you do not run under a daemon; say so.
agent_def:
# New definitions: agent_def

Tool `agent_def` makes agent definitions. A definition is a folder (`system.txt`, `tools.json`, `llm.json`, `interfaces.json`, ...); a new kind of agent = a copy of a template, edited.

One op per call:

- copy a stock template: `{"op": "new", "template": "agent-fsm", "path": "defs/helper"}` (templates: `agent-fsm`, `eca-claude`)
- copy any other definition folder: `{"op": "new", "from": "defs/helper", "path": "defs/helper2"}`
- check: `{"op": "check", "path": "defs/helper"}` (prints `{"problems": [...]}`; an empty list = OK)

Steps:

1. `new` from a template.
2. Edit the copy with your normal file tools: `system.txt` (who it is), `tools.json` (its tools), `llm.json` (its brain, like `{"model": "fake"}`).
3. `check` it.
4. Start it: `subagent` `{"op": "add", "def": "defs/helper", "name": "helper"}` (yours), or `agents_ctl` add (not yours).

Rules:

- `new` only copies: it starts nothing and changes no content. Relative tool paths in the copy's tools file are rewritten so they still point at the same tools.
- `path` must not exist yet; it can be anywhere you may write. Relative paths start at your workspace.
- `DefExists`: pick another `path`. `DefMissing`: the folder (`from`, or `path` for check) is not there. `DirectiveBad`: the `{"$env": ...}` could not be resolved (the variable is not set). `DefBad`: check found problems; fix the files it names and check again.
- Editing a definition affects every agent that uses it. To change only one agent, use `subagent` tools / llm on your child, or `self_tools` / `self_llm` on yourself.
thought:
# Small thought: one task, just the conclusion

The `thought` tool starts a disposable child agent, gives it one task and returns only a short conclusion; the child's tool exchanges do not enter your history. The child definition comes from the call parameter `from`; only when omitted does it use the default in the tool registration's `env.AOS_THOUGHT_FROM`.

Choosing a tool:

- `thought`: one step in a plan, returning one sentence after checking. By default it is removed after answering; no naming, follow-up or manual removal is needed.
- `subagent`: an assistant for an ongoing conversation. Name it, ask it questions, and `rm` it yourself.

Calls:

- With a configured default: `{"goal": "Find what time it is and say whether it is morning"}`.
- Choose another definition: `{"from": "helpers/reviewer", "goal": "Review the result and return one sentence"}`.
- Borrow your own tools: `{"goal": "Read the knowledge base and summarize endpoint packs", "tools": [{"name": "knowledge_read"}], "max_chars": 200}`.
- A → B → C: call once per step, passing the previous conclusion in `context`, for example `"context": ["Step A concluded: the config is in cfg/"]`.

Rules:

- Put the default in this agent's thought tool registration, for example `{"path": "../../lib/agent/thought", "env": {"AOS_THOUGHT_FROM": "helpers/basic"}}`. You can also use `--envs AOS_THOUGHT_FROM=helpers/basic` when registering the tool. The env value is passed literally, not resolved relative to the registry file; both `from` and this default resolve relative to your workspace `$AOS_WS`, while absolute paths are used as given. Store relative paths for portability. The definition must declare the `aos-agent` public interface. If neither is supplied, the result is `FromMissing`; no template is guessed. An explicitly blank value or wrong type gives `ArgumentsBad`, without falling back to the default.
- The child receives `goal` and `context` on top of its definition's existing settings. State clearly in `goal` what it should return.
- Tools: omitted `tools` keeps the definition's tool set; `[]` clears it; a list keeps only those tools. `{"name": "knowledge_read"}` without `path` borrows your own tool of that name; with `path`, that path is used. Overlays follow the definition's `interfaces.json` declarations.
- Brain: defaults to yours; `endpoint` can select another pack. If your brain settings cannot be read (for example, a sandbox cannot see the definition), an error is returned, commonly `InterfaceMissing`; you can supply `endpoint` explicitly.
- Depth is read from the startup environment's `AOS_THOUGHT_DEPTH` (unset means 0); the child starts with the parent's depth plus 1. Calling again at depth 2 gives `DepthExceeded`.
- `keep: true` stops and keeps the child after answering, appending `details: procs/<name>/` (relative to the daemon) to the conclusion. For a follow-up, first run `aos-agent ctl start --target <name>`, then `say`/`listen`.
- `AnswerMissing`: no answer within `timeout_s` (default 600; any finite positive number); the error line ends with `(details: ...)`, and the stack is kept for human inspection. `DepthExceeded`: the depth limit was reached; do this step yourself. `ToolMissing`: you do not have the same-named tool to borrow. `ArgumentsBad`: `goal` is missing or blank, or a parameter is invalid. `DaemonMissing`: `AOS_DAEMON` is unset or its directory does not exist. `DaemonFailed`: the daemon is configured and its directory exists, but no reply arrived within the timeout (it may be busy, paused or down). Do this step yourself or explain that it is temporarily unavailable; try at most once more later, without a retry loop.
